areas.label: Availability
areas.note: If this is red the server is down or a database is not usable — nothing else matters first.

areas.label: CPU
areas.threshold: WARN ≥ 80% · CRITICAL ≥ 90% — the collector's severity, held for half of the last hour; the value is the hour's average
areas.note: Sustained high CPU makes every query slower; check the top process and the heaviest queries. One sample at 95% is a moment, so the tile reads the hour (2026-10-26).
areas.detail: timed_statistics=FALSE on this instance: the database records no CPU time, so its CPU use cannot be read from it

areas.label: Memory
areas.threshold: WARN ≥ 85% · CRITICAL ≥ 95% used (report rule, on the last hour's average)
areas.note: A host short of memory swaps, and an engine short of cache reads the same pages from disk again and again.

areas.label: Disk space
areas.threshold: host: WARN ≥ 85% used · CRITICAL ≥ 95% used; the engine's own files by its collector's rule
areas.note: A full data or log volume stops writes: the database goes read-only or the instance stalls.

areas.label: Disk latency
areas.threshold: WARN ≥ 20 ms · CRITICAL ≥ 50 ms — report rule, the collector logs only. Over the last hour, from the stored counters
areas.note: Latency above ~20 ms per I/O means storage, not SQL, is the bottleneck. Graded on the last hour, from the file counters the store keeps; the latest interval and the last 24 hours are printed beside it, and the average since the engine started is printed and not graded.
areas.capacity: latest — / — ms · 1 h — / — ms · 24 h 0.0 / 0.0 ms (read / write)

areas.label: Storage activity
areas.threshold: WARN queue length ≥ 2 per spindle, held for half of the last hour — throughput and IOPS are logged, not judged
areas.note: How hard the storage is being worked. A high queue with low throughput is a storage limit; high throughput on its own is just a busy server.

areas.label: Blocking
areas.threshold: WARN any blocked session · CRITICAL ≥ 10 blocked or blocked ≥ 300 s
areas.note: One session holding a lock can stall an application entirely; find the head blocker.
areas.detail: Blocking ran and returned no rows

areas.label: Long-running queries
areas.note: A query running for an hour is usually a missing index, a bad plan, or a runaway job.
areas.detail: Long-running queries ran and returned no rows

areas.label: Backup
areas.threshold: per-database policy: required FULL/DIFF/LOG age from data/backup_policy.json
areas.note: Backup age is your worst-case data loss. A stale log backup means point-in-time recovery is not possible for that database.

areas.label: Failed jobs
areas.threshold: WARN any job failed since the last run
areas.note: A failed maintenance job is a backup, an index rebuild or a purge that silently did not happen.

areas.label: Temporary space
areas.threshold: WARN ≥ 85% used and < 2 GB free · CRITICAL ≥ 95% used and < 1 GB free
areas.note: Temporary space filling up fails sorts and hashes — often a single bad query.

areas.label: Security
areas.threshold: no sustained failed logins · no password older than the collector's threshold · no certificate expiring
areas.note: Thousands of failed logins a day is a credential being guessed or an RouteArchive retrying a dead one — and it fills the error log either way.

areas.label: HA / replication
areas.threshold: every replica CONNECTED and SYNCHRONIZED / streaming
areas.note: A replica that stopped synchronising is not a replica: failover would lose data.

areas.label: Sessions and processes
areas.threshold: WARN ≥ 80% of the processes / sessions limit · CRITICAL ≥ 90% — dead weight: WARN ≥ 10% of the process limit held by killed sessions or orphaned threads · CRITICAL ≥ 20%
areas.note: At the limit Oracle refuses every new connection (ORA-00020). A killed session or a thread with no session still holds its slot, so the ceiling can be reached by sessions that do no work.

areas.label: Tablespaces
areas.threshold: free space counting autoextend: WARN < 500 MB or < 5% · CRITICAL < 100 MB or < 2% — a segment at ≥ 90% of its extent limit is CRITICAL
areas.note: A tablespace with no room fails the next insert into anything stored in it (ORA-01653); a segment at its extent limit fails the same way with space to spare.

areas.label: SGA memory
areas.threshold: shared pool free: WARN < 25 MB · CRITICAL < 10 MB — buffer cache hit ratio: WARN < 90%
areas.note: A shared pool with nothing free ends in ORA-04031: statements can no longer be parsed. A low buffer cache hit ratio means blocks are read from disk again and again.

areas.label: Rollback segments
areas.note: Transactions queueing for a rollback segment header: there are too few segments for the number of concurrent writers.

areas.label: Invalid objects
areas.threshold: WARN any invalid object · CRITICAL any unusable index
areas.note: Invalid code raises ORA-04068 when it is called, not when it broke; an unusable index fails every DML on its table unless SKIP_UNUSABLE_INDEXES is on.
